definitions.explanation: A suffix attached to nouns referring to people to indicate plurality. Can also indicate a group including the named person.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもたちは{新|あたら}しい{寝巻|ねまき}を{買|か}ってもらって{喜|よろこ}んでいた。
examples.english: The children were delighted to have new pajamas bought for them.

examples.japanese: {友|とも}だちたちと{遊|あそ}ぶ。
{私|わたし}たちは{日本人|にほんじん}です。
{田中|たなか}さんたちが{来|き}た。
examples.notes: Name + たち = the named person and their group

notes:
USAGE:
・Attaches to nouns referring to people
・{子|こ}どもたち (children)
・{学生|がくせい}たち (students)
・{私|わたし}たち (we)
・{彼|かれ}ら vs. {彼|かれ}たち (both mean "they" but たち is softer)

NOTE ON NAMES:
・{田中|たなか}さんたち = Tanaka-san and their group/friends/family
・This usage implies "the person and people associated with them"

WRITING:
Usually written in hiragana, but can be written as {達|たち} in formal contexts.

SIMILAR SUFFIXES:
・たち - general plural for people
・ら - slightly more casual/rough plural
・{方|がた} - polite plural ({先生|せんせい}{方|がた} = teachers)
